# hg debug

**What this page tells you:** every `hg debug` subcommand, with its arguments, flags and defaults.

The passive debug observer.

## Synopsis

```text
hg debug webhook enable
hg debug webhook status
hg debug webhook tail [flags]
hg debug webhook clear
hg debug webhook disable
```

`--json` prints one JSON document on stdout; narration goes to stderr.

## Description

Manage the host webhook sink and read its JSONL. The router mirrors metadata-only lifecycle records here only when its emitted values carry the URL (`topology emit --observer-url`) — Git decides, never this command.

## `hg debug webhook enable`

```text
hg debug webhook enable
```

Start the host webhook sink.

## `hg debug webhook status`

```text
hg debug webhook status
```

Sink state and url.

## `hg debug webhook tail`

```text
hg debug webhook tail [flags]
```

Read the captured records.

| Flag | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--tail` | `<n>` | `20` | How many records. |
| `--planes` | `<plane,..>` | — | Filter by plane. |

## `hg debug webhook clear`

```text
hg debug webhook clear
```

Truncate the capture file.

## `hg debug webhook disable`

```text
hg debug webhook disable
```

Stop the sink.
